# Design — Two Branches

Turning the diff into a therapeutic. The two branches have different evaluability and different economics of manufacture. Immune ([immune/index.md](immune/index.md)) is the fastest personalized loop today; genetic ([genetic/index.md](genetic/index.md)) works for point drivers and mostly ex vivo. The genetic guide oracle is delegated to the onco-target-design domain; the mRNA construct oracle to mrna-design.

### Subfolders

- [genetic/](genetic/index.md): Oncolytic virus, CRISPR/base/prime, ASO/siRNA. Allele-specific targeting is real for *specific* drivers (KRAS G12x, fusion breakpoints, HPV E6/E7) — not "any mutation." Mostly ex vivo (allogeneic CAR-T with CRISPR knockout) or organs you can reach (liver); direct in-vivo editing of solid-tumor cells is not clinically achieved (blocked by the delivery wall). The sequence-level guide/off-target oracle lives in the paired **onco-target-design** domain — point there for guide design. (0 files)
- [immune/](immune/index.md): The fastest personalized loop today: neoantigen mRNA/peptide vaccines (mRNA-4157, autogene cevumeran), adoptive cell therapy (CAR-T/TCR-T/TIL), and off-the-shelf engagers (BiTE/ICI). Computable: somatic variants, HLA, binding/presentation, mRNA construct design (delegated to mrna-design). Empirical: immunogenicity, off-tumor toxicity, persistence/trafficking, response of "cold" tumors. Rate-limited by neoantigen immunogenicity (see [walls/index.md](../../walls/index.md)). (0 files)
